hook: One small black hole merger can wipe out 2 to 3 orders of magnitude of a dark matter spike.
summary: Dark matter spikes around massive black holes could be spotted through gravitational-wave dephasing, but mergers destroy them. Simulations of binary inspirals show even a 0.005 mass-ratio merger cuts central density sharply. Combined with merger histories from the Horizon-AGN simulation, this limits detectable spikes to black holes of 10^6 to 5x10^7 solar masses. The results are simulation-based and assume spikes form in the first place.
title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
